title: Negotiated desktop bridge admission and replay lifetime

x-semantics.negotiation: Agent advertises protocol_version=3. Missing version selects legacy v2; explicit unsupported versions fail with 426 before registration or acknowledgement. Once v3 is observed, the agent refuses downgrade within that connection run.
x-semantics.expiry: expires_at is the original server creation time plus pickup TTL, never extended by redelivery. Server_time anchors a monotonic agent clock; expired commands never execute even after their replay record is reclaimed. The agent conservatively charges request elapsed time when anchoring the clock so a delayed first response cannot execute expired work; extremely short pickup TTLs may be refused early.
x-semantics.replay: Keep running and unacknowledged IDs. Reclaim only expired finite-deadline IDs after completion and acknowledgement. Legacy IDs remain pinned until restart without changing legacy demand-driven admission. This is process-local deduplication, not durable exactly-once execution.
x-semantics.flow_control: Agent reports execution_slots on every poll. Server delivers no more normal work than those slots, counting claimed nonterminal work; cancellation bypasses execution slots. Every response stays within command_batch. Resident outboxes scale independently; wire prefixes and per-frame limits retain the result/stream floors. Uploads with output acknowledge without long-poll delay, and the agent drains a remaining prefix immediately. Slots are resource-derived advisory server delivery credits; the agent does not reject already-issued work for a local worker quota. Memory overflow spools privately, preserving output until acknowledgement or joined shutdown.
x-semantics.authority: The authenticated server owner and device claim remain the settlement authority. The agent independently validates target_agent_id before acknowledging a batch or dispatching controls. Credentials never authorize a discovered route.
